actions.name: ButtonStart_Click
actions.purpose: Downloads Microsoft's policy definitions package, unpacks it and moves the files into the chosen folder.

context.scope: Action started by a person in the DownloadAdmx screen of Getting Microsoft policy definitions: Downloads Microsoft's policy definitions package, unpacks it and moves the files into the chosen folder.
rules: When files are moved into a folder, the folder is created if missing and every file already there with the same name is deleted first and then replaced by the new one, with no backup. Only files directly in the source folder are moved. A failure part-way leaves some files replaced and others not. (PolicyPlus/DownloadAdmx.vb:52)

For an administrator, each folder handed to the file move that already exists, the destination itself and any existing language folder, has its ownership taken; a language folder created during the move instead inherits permissions from the folder above. Every moved file, including the template files in the destination, is reset to inherit permissions. A standard user changes no permissions. A failure here ends the download with "Failed to move the ADMX files.", not the take-control message. (PolicyPlus/DownloadAdmx.vb:55)

Starting the download always fetches one fixed Microsoft package, the Windows 11 September 2026 Update (26H2) administrative templates, into a scratch folder under the person's local application data as "W11Admx.msi"; the person cannot choose another version. (PolicyPlus/DownloadAdmx.vb:83)

The downloaded package is unpacked with the Windows installer tool; if the tool ends with a non-zero code the download stops with "Failed to extract the package." and the package is kept. When it succeeds, the downloaded package file is deleted. (PolicyPlus/DownloadAdmx.vb:89)

Before any file is moved, when the folder written in the destination box already exists and the person is an administrator, ownership of it is taken and Administrators are given full control. This applies to whatever folder text is in the box, not only the Windows folder; a standard user skips it. A failure ends the download with "Failed to take control of the destination." and nothing is moved. (PolicyPlus/DownloadAdmx.vb:94)

The template files are moved into the destination, then the language files for the person's regional format language (the culture of the regional settings, which can differ from the display language) are moved into a folder of that name if the package holds one. Unless that language is en-US, the English files are also moved into an en-US folder as a fallback; if the package has no en-US folder, the download stops with "Failed to move the ADMX files." after the destination files were already replaced. (PolicyPlus/DownloadAdmx.vb:103)

While a download runs, the start button, close button, destination box and browse button are all disabled, so a second download cannot be started and the destination cannot change; they are enabled again when it ends. (PolicyPlus/DownloadAdmx.vb:22)

After a successful download the scratch folder is deleted, the person is asked "ADMX files downloaded successfully. Open them now?", and the destination is reported as the new policy folder only if they answer Yes; either answer closes the window as done. (PolicyPlus/DownloadAdmx.vb:117)
unconfirmed: For the capability: The package at the fixed Microsoft address is assumed to still hold the template folder at the expected path and an en-US language folder, and to unpack with a zero exit code. A different layout makes every download fail at the unpack or move step. If wrong: Downloads fail with a step message, and the fixed path and link must be changed in a rebuild.

actions.name: AcquireADMXFilesToolStripMenuItem_Click
actions.purpose: Opens the download window and loads the downloaded definitions.

context.scope: Action started by a person in the Main screen of Getting Microsoft policy definitions: Opens the download window and loads the downloaded definitions.
rules: When a language file has no policy resources section, or its revision is missing or not a number, the file is refused as invalid and its template file is not loaded. (PolicyPlus/AdmlFile.vb:18)

A template file is refused as invalid when any of these is missing or unreadable: the policy definitions section; a namespace entry's prefix or namespace; a superseded-ADM file name; a minimum revision (missing or not a number); a support rule's name or display name; a support reference or range without its reference, or a version bound that is not a whole number; a product's name, display name or version index; a category's name or display name; a category's parent entry or its reference when the category has content; a policy's name, display name, key or class; a policy's category or supported-on reference; a number value's value; a list item's value name; a choice item's display name; or an option's id. (PolicyPlus/AdmxFile.vb:20)
The namespace of a template is the one listed as its target; each prefix a template declares must be unique, and a repeated prefix refuses the file as invalid. (PolicyPlus/AdmxFile.vb:24)

A language file's text table is read only from its first text table, and each text is kept under its id; when the same text id appears twice, the file is refused as invalid and its template file is not loaded. (PolicyPlus/AdmlFile.vb:29)

A template's superseded-ADM file name and minimum language revision are read when present; a superseded entry without a file name, or a minimum revision that is missing or not a number, refuses the template as invalid. (PolicyPlus/AdmxFile.vb:30)

When a template file cannot be parsed as XML, it is refused with the message "Couldn't load <path>: The ADMX XML couldn't be parsed: <detail>."; any other read problem is refused with "The ADMX is invalid: <detail>". (PolicyPlus/AdmxBundle.vb:37)

A language file's screen layouts are read only from its first presentation table; when the same layout id appears twice, the file is refused as invalid and its template file is not loaded. (PolicyPlus/AdmlFile.vb:40)

When a template file's namespace is already held by a template file loaded earlier, it is refused with "The <namespace> namespace is already owned by a different ADMX file", so the same file cannot be added twice. (PolicyPlus/AdmxBundle.vb:44)
